info.title: Querycraft Gateway API
info.description: Adapter B: the JSON HTTP surface the Querycraft client talks to. Response schemas mirror contracts/*.schema.json where a contract file exists; the rest are defined here.

tags.name: system
tags.description: Liveness, advertised capabilities, metrics and diagnostics.

tags.name: auth
tags.description: Local accounts and session cookies. A bearer token is also issued for API clients.

tags.name: environment
tags.description: The learner's writable workspace and its reset.

get.summary: Liveness probe that also reports the engine version.
Advertised execution limits and isolation mode.
Prometheus text exposition of request, statement and pool metrics.
get.description: Unlabelled series arrive without braces. Labels are a bounded set (route patterns, method, status class, error code), so scraping never grows unbounded series. The pool and readiness gauges are sampled at scrape time.

get.summary: Measured readiness, versions, pool state and sandbox facts.
get.description: Never includes a DSN, password or hash. The learner subsection is read over the restricted connection, so it reports the privileges learner SQL actually holds. Requires a session.

post.summary: Execute a SQL statement in a read-only transaction and return its rows.

400.description: A malformed or empty body is the ErrorEnvelope (EMPTY_QUERY or QUERY_SYNTAX_ERROR). A statement that ran and failed is a QueryResult whose error.code is a stable code (EMPTY_QUERY, QUERY_SYNTAX_ERROR, QUERY_RUNTIME_ERROR, QUERY_TIMEOUT, RESULT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE, DIALECT_MISMATCH).

post.summary: Capture an EXPLAIN plan, optionally executing the statement with ANALYZE.
post.description: The response is the PlanBundle described by contracts/plan.schema.json: 'summary' and 'environment' carry the deterministic, gradeable facts (node types, relations, indexes, the planner's own row estimates, engine version, row counts and planner settings) and 'plan' is the engine's own JSON plan, reported verbatim and never graded. 'timing_precision' names what the numbers beside it are worth. A graded assertion never reads a timing. EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement, so it requires a signed-in learner's writable environment and is refused with ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE for an anonymous caller rather than silently downgraded to a plain EXPLAIN; with no database the route reports ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE and never invents a plan.

400.description: A malformed or empty body is the ErrorEnvelope (EMPTY_QUERY or QUERY_SYNTAX_ERROR). A plan that could not be captured is a PlanBundle whose error.code is a stable code (EMPTY_QUERY, QUERY_SYNTAX_ERROR, QUERY_RUNTIME_ERROR, QUERY_TIMEOUT, RESULT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE, EVALUATION_ERROR).

post.summary: Run the learner's SQL and grade it against an exercise contract.

200.description: Evaluation result. The embedded qr carries any execution error.

400.description: The request body was empty or malformed JSON; the body is the ErrorEnvelope (EMPTY_QUERY or QUERY_SYNTAX_ERROR).

get.summary: Describe the caller's writable learner workspace.
get.description: A signed-in learner gets their own database, copied from the sealed template and created on first use. An anonymous caller has no workspace and is told so honestly (exists=false, writable=false) rather than being shown the shared dataset as if it were theirs. A gateway with no database answers 503 ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE.

503.description: No workspace can be provided (no database, or the capacity cap is reached); the body is the ErrorEnvelope with code ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE.

post.summary: Restore the sealed dataset, discarding the learner's own changes.
post.description: Drops the caller's environment database and copies the sealed template again. Destructive to the caller's own workspace only. Requires a signed-in account; an anonymous caller is refused with AUTH_REQUIRED. When the course parameter names a stored course, that course's own setup statements are applied to the restored workspace in order, so the learner's database is the one the course's exercises were verified against; setup_statements reports how many were applied. A course is resolved owner-scoped, and a course id that is not the caller's is refused with 404 NOT_FOUND so it cannot be probed for existence.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: Which workspace to restore. Absent, "" and "commerce" all restore the caller's challenge workspace; "perf" restores the plan lab, which is a separate database so a re-indexed plan lesson cannot change the plan a challenge lesson is graded on. A name this gateway does not serve is refused with ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE naming the datasets it does.

parameters.name: course
parameters.description: A stored course whose setup should be re-applied after the template is copied, so the learner's environment equals the one its exercises were verified in. Resolved owner-scoped; an id that is not the caller's, or does not exist, is refused with 404 NOT_FOUND and applies nothing. A course cannot be combined with the "perf" dataset: a course runs in its own workspace, so that request is refused with 400.

parameters.name: dialect
parameters.description: Which engine's workspace to restore. Absent means postgresql, so a client that has never heard of the field keeps the behaviour it had. "sqlite" restores the learner's SQLite database file to the committed fixture; only a signed-in account has one. A dialect this gateway does not serve is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH. The dialect matters because the two workspaces are different things — a database versus a file — so resetting one while the learner is looking at the other would report a restore that did not happen.

200.description: The workspace was restored; duration_ms is the measured end-to-end reset time in milliseconds and setup_statements is how many of the named course's setup statements were applied (0 when no course was named).

400.description: The request named a course together with the perf dataset, a dataset this gateway does not serve, or a dialect it cannot reset (DIALECT_MISMATCH). The body is the route's own ErrorEnvelope ({ok:false,error}), not a QueryResult — a reset is not a statement.

404.description: The request named a course that does not exist or is not the caller's; nothing was reset and nothing was applied.

503.description: No workspace can be provided; the body is the ErrorEnvelope with code ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE.

post.summary: Apply a stored course's own setup to the learner's workspace.
post.description: Ensures the caller's workspace exists and applies the named stored course's setup statements to it, so the learner's database is the one the course's exercises were verified against. A course is resolved owner-scoped, and a course id that is not the caller's is refused with 404 NOT_FOUND so it cannot be probed for existence. The route is idempotent: a stored course's setup statements are not idempotent themselves, so the gateway records that the setup was applied beside the workspace and a second call for the same course and workspace is a cheap no-op reporting setup_statements 0. A reset clears the record, so the course is prepared again. With no database the route answers 503 ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE and the course still opens.

parameters.name: course
parameters.description: The stored course whose setup should be applied. Resolved owner-scoped; an id that is not the caller's, or does not exist, is refused with 404 NOT_FOUND and applies nothing.

parameters.name: dialect
parameters.description: Which engine's workspace to prepare. Absent means postgresql, so a client that has never heard of the field prepares the challenge workspace. "sqlite" prepares the learner's SQLite file; only a signed-in account has one. A dialect this gateway does not serve is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH.

200.description: The workspace was prepared; setup_statements is how many of the course's setup statements were applied by this call (0 when a previous call already applied them).

400.description: No course was named, or the request named a dialect this gateway cannot prepare. The body is the route's own ErrorEnvelope ({ok:false,error}).

404.description: The request named a course that does not exist or is not the caller's; nothing was prepared.

500.description: A setup statement failed; the workspace was not prepared and the mark was left unset, so a retry runs the setup again.

503.description: No workspace can be provided; the body is the ErrorEnvelope with code ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE.

get.summary: List a dataset's tables, columns and preview rows.

parameters.name: dialect
parameters.description: Which engine's workspace to describe. Absent means postgresql. "sqlite" introspects the SQLite workspace over the executor seam — the learner's own file when signed in, the shared fixture otherwise — so a SQLite chapter's drawer lists SQLite relations and their declared types (affinities), not PostgreSQL's.

get.summary: Load the signed-in account's progress snapshot for a course.

200.description: Snapshot (null when nothing is stored yet).

put.summary: Replace the stored progress snapshot for a course with arbitrary JSON.

400.description: Body was empty or not valid JSON.
The body was not a JSON object or carried no event id.

post.summary: Generate a course, one chapter at a time, through the chapter agent.
post.description: The model is an untrusted content generator; the gateway is the policy. The run asks for a small outline first, stores it as a 'building' course, and then holds one conversation in which the model hands in one chapter per save_chapter tool call. Each chapter is validated with the same gates a challenge is and run in the course's own scratch environment before it is appended to the stored plan, so GET /courses/{id} answers with the chapters that already verified while the rest are still being written. 'stages' reports what the pipeline did, and a course job's live progress is 'chapters_planned' / 'chapters_verified' / 'current_chapter'. 'status' is 'active' only for a course whose every stored exercise verified; a chapter the model cannot repair is dropped and reported; a run in which nothing verified is 'rejected' and stores nothing. Set 'require_approval' to have the run stop after the outline: the response status is then 'awaiting_approval', the stored 'building' course is the index to approve, and POST /courses/{id}/build continues it into the chapter phase. The pause is opt-in: without the flag the run is one request, outline into chapters. Requires a session. Answers 503 when AI is off or the gateway is at its concurrency limit, 400 for an invalid request. A generation takes minutes, so a client that cannot wait sends Prefer: respond-async (or async=1) and polls GET /generation/{id} instead of holding the request open; that path answers 202 with the job id.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: Send a Prefer header of 'respond-async' (or pass async=1) to get a 202 with a job id instead of waiting for the envelope. The blocking envelope is the default.

202.description: The run was accepted and continues in the background. Poll GET /generation/{id}.

400.description: A malformed or empty body is the ErrorEnvelope (AI_INVALID_REQUEST). A request the pipeline refused is an AIOutcome.

422.description: Generation ran and nothing was activated; the outcome names the stage that refused.

503.description: AI is off, the database cannot verify, or the gateway is at capacity.

get.summary: List the caller's stored generated courses, newest first.
get.description: Only the session's own courses are returned; the depot is scoped on write, so the filter lives in the handler. With AI off the answer is 503 and 'courses' is an empty array, never an invented row.

200.description: Courses that survived activation, newest first.

503.description: AI is off; the body is an AICourseList with ok=false and an empty 'courses'.

get.summary: List every stored course, every owner (administrators).
get.description: The course inventory the manage surface renders: every stored record with its owner id and status, including 'building', 'awaiting_approval' and 'interrupted' courses no learner can see. A signed-in learner is refused with 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED; the role lives on the stored account and public signups never receive it. With AI off the answer is 503 and 'courses' is an empty array, never an invented row. Detail routes stay owner-scoped: a course that is not the caller's is still 404 there, so an id cannot be probed for existence.

200.description: Every stored course, newest first, with owner ids.

403.description: Signed in without the administrator role (ADMIN_REQUIRED).

503.description: AI is off; the body is an AICourseList with ok=false and an empty 'courses'.

get.summary: The caller's client preferences (theme, custom themes).
get.description: One JSON document per account under the 'ui' key. It is what makes a theme follow the account across devices; a device that has never saved preferences gets ok with null preferences, never an invented default. The body is client-owned JSON: the gateway stores and returns it, it does not interpret it.

200.description: The stored preference document, or null when the account has none.

put.description: Replaces the account's 'ui' document wholesale. Owner-scoped: the account comes from the session, never the body. The document is client-owned JSON (theme id, custom theme token sets); the gateway stores it and does not interpret it. Bounded by the same body limit as every write.

200.description: Saved; the response echoes ok with the stored document.

400.description: Malformed JSON or the document exceeds the body limit.

get.summary: The live AI configuration and where it came from (administrators).
get.description: Reports provider, model, base_url, timeout and key_set (the key itself never travels back in a body). Source is 'database' when an administrator saved a configuration through PUT /admin/ai and the boot path applied it, or 'boot' when the config file's provider is live and nothing has been saved here. A signed-in learner is refused with 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED.

403.description: Signed in without the administrator role (ADMIN_REQUIRED).

put.summary: Save and apply an AI configuration while the gateway runs (administrators).
put.description: Persists the configuration under the store's 'ai' key (it survives a restart: the boot path applies it over the config file's provider) and swaps the running configuration. Provider is one of 'off', 'fake', 'openai-compatible', 'pi-ai'; the openai-compatible provider requires base_url and model. 'pi-ai' runs every completion through pi's unified multi-provider API (Anthropic, OpenAI completions and responses, Gemini): a model ref such as anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5 resolves against the embedded model catalog, or set base_url and model to target any custom OpenAI-compatible server. An empty key keeps the stored one, so a round-trip through the manage surface never demands the key again. The run budget follows the boot derivation from the saved call timeout. Requests and jobs submitted after the save build their services from the new configuration; a run already in flight keeps the provider it started with. Nothing here touches the config file: the file is the boot document, the store is the runtime one. A signed-in learner is refused with 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED.

400.description: Unknown provider, an openai-compatible configuration missing base_url or model, or a negative timeout (AI_INVALID_REQUEST).

403.description: Signed in without the administrator role (ADMIN_REQUIRED).

get.summary: The embedded model catalog (administrators).
get.description: Every chat model the pi catalog knows, as provider + model id + display name — the list the manage surface's provider picker offers. From the same generated catalog the pi-ai provider resolves model refs against, sourced from models.dev. A signed-in learner is refused with 403 ADMIN_REQUIRED.

403.description: Signed in without the administrator role (ADMIN_REQUIRED).

get.summary: Read one stored course with the evidence that admitted it.
get.description: A course that belongs to another learner is reported as 404, never 403, so its existence cannot be confirmed.

404.description: No such course, or it belongs to another learner.

put.summary: Edit a stored course's title, subtitle and chapter headings.
put.description: Only the authored fields may change: the course title and subtitle, and a chapter's title and summary. The exercises, the setup plan and the pipeline's provenance were verified by generation and are not editable here. Every chapter id must name a chapter the stored plan already has, and at least one field must differ from it. A course that belongs to another learner is reported as 404, never 403, so its existence cannot be confirmed.

200.description: The edit was stored; the body is the updated record.

400.description: A malformed body is the ErrorEnvelope (AI_INVALID_REQUEST). A body that names an unknown chapter, exceeds a field limit, or changes nothing is also refused with AI_INVALID_REQUEST and a message naming the field.

404.description: No such course, or it belongs to another learner.

delete.description: Removes the generated plan only. Learner attempts and progress are the learner's data and are not touched. A course that belongs to another learner is reported as 404, never 403.

404.description: No such course, or it belongs to another learner.

post.summary: Approve a paused course and build its chapters.
post.description: Continues a course that stopped at 'awaiting_approval', or one an interrupted build left behind: the stored outline is reloaded, the chapter conversation is rebuilt from the request stored beside it, and the chapter phase runs to completion, activating the course exactly as a default run would. A chapter that already verified is not re-written. The route is owner-scoped: a course that belongs to another learner is reported as 404, never 403. A course that is not still being built is refused with 409, because re-running a finished course is not what this route is for. A continuation takes minutes, so it accepts the same Prefer: respond-async (or async=1) ask as /courses/generate and answers 202 with the job id; the blocking envelope is the default.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: Send a Prefer header of 'respond-async' (or pass async=1) to get a 202 with a job id instead of waiting for the envelope.

202.description: The continuation was accepted and runs in the background. Poll GET /generation/{id}.

201.description: The course was built and activated, exactly as a default run would.

404.description: No such course, or it belongs to another learner.

409.description: The course is not awaiting approval: only a course that is still being built can be continued.

422.description: The continuation ran and nothing was activated; the outcome names the stage that refused.

503.description: AI is off, the database cannot verify, or the gateway is at capacity.

get.summary: Poll a generation that was submitted with Prefer: respond-async.
get.description: The body is the job's own view: a live copy of the pipeline's stages while the run is going, and the pipeline's final report once it is over. A course job also carries its chapter progress ('chapters_planned', 'chapters_verified', 'current_chapter') and 'chapters', the per-chapter report in course order. A job that belongs to another learner is reported as 404, never 403, so an id cannot be probed for existence. The stored record, not the job, is the durable thing: a course job names its course_id as soon as the outline is stored — that course reads as 'building' from GET /courses/{id} and carries the chapters that already verified — and a challenge job names its challenge_id once the challenge was stored. A refused run names neither, because it stored nothing.

200.description: The job view, whatever state the run is in.

404.description: No such job, or it belongs to another learner.

503.description: AI is off; the body is an AIJobResponse with ok=false and job=null.

post.summary: Generate one challenge through the 11.1 pipeline.
post.description: Same contract and same statuses as /courses/generate.

parameters.name: Prefer
parameters.description: Send a Prefer header of 'respond-async' (or pass async=1) to get a 202 with a job id instead of waiting for the envelope. The blocking envelope is the default.

202.description: The run was accepted and continues in the background. Poll GET /generation/{id}.

400.description: A malformed or empty body is the ErrorEnvelope (AI_INVALID_REQUEST). A request the pipeline refused is an AIOutcome.

422.description: Generation ran and nothing was activated.

503.description: AI is off, the database cannot verify, or the gateway is at capacity.

get.summary: List stored generated challenges, newest first.
Read one stored challenge with the evidence that admitted it.

200.description: The stored record, in the {ok, challenge} envelope.

post.description: Removes the generated definition only. Learner attempts are the learner's data and are not touched.

post.summary: Review the learner's own query on demand.
post.description: The critique never contains the reference solution.

post.summary: Report a defect in a challenge.
post.description: The claimed defect is reproduced by execution before any patch is proposed, and 'applied' stays false until the learner approves the patch.

200.description: A verdict, with evidence for either outcome.

post.summary: Approve or reject a proposed patch.
post.description: The approver is taken from the session, never from the body. An unapproved patch is refused with 409.

post.summary: Ask the tutor about the learner's own query, as a conversation or a one-shot hint.
post.description: The tutor sees the learner's SQL, the gateway's own run of it, the dataset schema, the result contract and, after an attempt, the expected result. It never sees the reference query: the gateway keeps that only to discard a reply that contains it. The client sends facts; the gateway assembles the context and reports a summary of what it saw in `context`. A zero-turn request behaves like the one-shot inline hint.

200.description: A tutor turn, with a summary of the context it saw.

400.description: The request names no exercise, exceeds the turn or context bounds, or carries an unknown turn role (AI_INVALID_REQUEST).

429.description: The account spent its tutor budget (AI_RATE_LIMITED).

get.summary: List the caller's generation runs, newest first.
get.description: Each generation run leaves a transcript: every provider message, tool call and tool result, in order, attributed to the run, the kind (challenge or course), the owner and the terminal outcome. The transcript is redacted before it is stored (a credential never reaches it) and bounded (a runaway run cannot bloat the database), so a stored run is a prefix of the conversation when the bound was hit — 'truncated' says so. This route returns summaries, newest first, capped at 100; another learner's runs are never listed.

503.description: No generation service (and so no transcript store) is configured.

get.summary: Read one generation run's transcript.
get.description: The whole stored conversation for one run: every message, tool call and tool result in order, with the run's kind, owner, status and error. The owner is the session's account and is not carried in the body. A run belonging to another account is reported 404, never 403, so an id cannot be probed for existence.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The run id: a job id from POST /courses/generate?async=1 or POST /challenges/generate?async=1, or the id minted for a blocking run.

200.description: The run's transcript, wrapped in the ok/run envelope.

404.description: No such run, or it belongs to another account.

503.description: No generation service (and so no transcript store) is configured.

post.summary: Create a learner account and start a session.
post.description: Public signups always receive the learner role; admin is not self-service. Sets the qc_session cookie and returns the same session token in the body for API clients.

400.description: Email, name or password failed validation.

post.description: An unknown email and a wrong password return the same 401 so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts. Repeated failures from one address against one account are refused with 429 AUTH_RATE_LIMITED (bounded per (address, email); a success clears the count). Sets the qc_session cookie and returns the same session token in the body for API clients.

429.description: Too many failed sign-in attempts for this address and account (AUTH_RATE_LIMITED). The Retry-After header carries whole seconds until the window ends. The body does not distinguish a known from an unknown address.

Retry-After.description: Whole seconds until the fixed window ends.

get.summary: Return the account behind the bearer token.
This OpenAPI document.

200.description: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this gateway.

get.summary: Swagger UI that renders this OpenAPI document.

bearerAuth.description: Opaque session token from /auth/login or /auth/signup, sent in the Authorization header as a Bearer token. It wins over the cookie when both are present.

cookieAuth.name: qc_session
cookieAuth.description: Session cookie set by /auth/login and /auth/signup (HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Secure over TLS) and cleared by /auth/logout. A cookie-authenticated mutating request is also required to look same-origin through its Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site header, or it is refused with 403 CSRF_REFUSED.

type.description: PostgreSQL type name, e.g. int8 or text.

dialect.description: The machine-readable dialect of the engine that produced this result. A chapter declares one dialect; a result from the other is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH rather than graded.

Limits.description: Per-request caps; zero values fall back to the server defaults.

dialect.description: The dialect to run the statement on. Absent means postgresql, the default dialect (ADR 0004), so an existing client is unchanged. A dialect this gateway does not serve is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH naming the dialects it does serve.

dataset.description: The fixture to run against: commerce (the shared read-only dataset, or the caller's own workspace when signed in) or perf (the larger plan fixture, always in the caller's own writable environment, so a CREATE INDEX cannot touch the challenge workspace). Absent, "", and "commerce" all mean commerce. A request that carries exercise.perf and names no dataset also routes to perf. The perf dataset is a PostgreSQL lab, so it is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH for another dialect; an unknown dataset is refused with ENVIRONMENT_UNAVAILABLE naming the datasets this gateway serves.

Exercise.description: The exercise facts POST /answers/evaluate grades with. The evaluator reads exactly three grading inputs: result_contract, reference_solution, and an optional pre-computed result. It does not read expected_result, expected_rows, checks, contract or solution; a body carrying them is graded as if they were absent. The authored id, version, lesson_id, type, prompt, setup, hints and difficulty travel but are not grading inputs. perf is read only to route an exercise with no dataset to the perf fixture.

dialect.description: The dialect this exercise's contract was written for.

result_contract.description: The result contract the evaluator reads. This is the only contract spelling it reads.

reference_solution.description: The query the gateway executes to derive the expected rows when result is absent. This is the only reference spelling it reads.

result.description: A pre-computed expected result. When present the gateway compares against it instead of running the reference.

perf.description: A PerfContract (contracts/perf-contract.schema.json). It is not graded here; its presence with no dataset routes the request to the perf fixture.

dialect.description: The dialect to run and grade the answer on. Absent means postgresql. Grading a SQLite answer against a PostgreSQL contract (or the reverse) is refused with DIALECT_MISMATCH rather than silently graded.

dataset.description: The fixture the answer is graded against: commerce (the shared read-only dataset, or the caller's own workspace when signed in) or perf (the larger plan fixture, always in the caller's own writable environment). Absent, "", and "commerce" all mean commerce; exercise.perf with no dataset also routes to perf. This is what a plans-course exercise needs: its authored result was written against perf rows, so grading it on commerce would compare the answer to the wrong table.

code.description: Feedback code for this check; the gateway clamps unknown codes to VALUE_MISMATCH.

Environment.description: The caller's learner workspace (ADR 0003). exists and writable are always present; the rest are facts read from the environment when it exists.

database.description: The environment database name; derived from the account id, never interpolated from it.

exists.description: Whether the caller's environment database currently exists.

writable.description: Whether a learner statement may write. False is correct for the anonymous shared dataset.

tables.description: Tables in the dataset schema, present only when the environment exists.

idle_until.description: When an idle environment is reaped if it goes unused.

duration_ms.description: Measured end-to-end reset time in milliseconds.

setup_statements.description: How many of the named course's setup statements were applied. 0 when the request named no course; the reset fails instead of reporting a partial application.
How many of the course's setup statements this call applied. 0 when a previous call already applied them; the prepare fails instead of reporting a partial application.

engine.description: The dialect of the executor that answers /query with no dialect field: the default dialect.

dialects.description: Every dialect this gateway can route a statement to, in stable order. A probe reads this rather than assuming one engine.

admin_password_empty.description: True only when the seeded default administrator can be signed in with an empty password (a loopback-only local-development install). The sign-in screen shows its local-admin hint for this boolean and no other reason. It is a boolean, never a password or a hash.

isolation.description: How a statement's writes are isolated, named for both callers because the answer differs by caller. An anonymous statement runs read-only against the shared dataset; a signed-in learner's runs in their own writable workspace (a PostgreSQL environment per ADR 0003, or their own SQLite file per ADR 0006).

anonymous.description: The isolation an anonymous caller's statement runs under. Currently read_only_tx.

signed_in.description: The isolation a signed-in caller's statement runs under. Currently writable_workspace.

writable.description: Whether this gateway can give a signed-in learner a writable workspace at all. False means a signed-in statement still runs read-only.

dialects.description: The dialects this gateway can run, in stable order. PostgreSQL is always present and is the default. A client disables a chapter whose dialect is missing from this list and names the one action that fixes it.

writable.description: Whether this gateway can give a signed-in learner a writable workspace: a per-account PostgreSQL environment (ADR 0003) or a per-account SQLite file. It says nothing about the caller: a client combines it with whether it holds a session to decide if EXPLAIN ANALYZE and DDL are available.

PlanCapability.description: What the M5 plan lab offers, so a client can hide the Explain button instead of probing for a failure. 'available' is false when the gateway has no database; 'analyze_requires_auth' is true because EXPLAIN ANALYZE executes the statement (ADR 0003).

PlanRequest.description: The POST /explain body. 'exercise.perf' is the PerfContract from contracts/perf-contract.schema.json; the gateway reads its 'engine' to refuse a chapter authored for another dialect, and the plan is graded against the rest of it in the browser and in backend/internal/perf.

analyze.description: False (the default) only plans. True runs EXPLAIN ANALYZE and requires a writable environment.

dialect.description: The dialect the plan is for. Absent means postgresql. The plan lab captures PostgreSQL plans only (ADR 0004: SQLite has no EXPLAIN ANALYZE), so another dialect is refused with EVALUATION_ERROR and a sentence naming PostgreSQL.

dataset.description: commerce (the shared read-only dataset, or the caller's own workspace when signed in) or perf (the larger plan fixture, always in the caller's own environment). Absent, "", and "commerce" all mean commerce; exercise.perf with no dataset also routes to perf.

PlanBundle.description: The plan result described by contracts/plan.schema.json, the single source of truth for this shape; the summary below names the fields a client keys off rather than restating the contract.

AIAvailability.description: Whether the AI lab can run, and why not when it cannot. Clients hide the lab when 'available' is false and show 'reason' instead.

exercise_count.description: How many exercises the run asks for. The service clamps the value to this range; both courses and challenges read the normalized count.

require_approval.description: Course only. When true the run stops after the outline is validated and stored: the response status is 'awaiting_approval' and POST /courses/{id}/build continues it. Off (and absent) by default, which is a single request that runs outline into chapters.

AIEvidence.description: Measured facts from the run. Zero means the check did not run or found nothing.

AIArtifact.description: A challenge the service has verified. Only ever written to the active set after every pipeline stage passed.

AIOutcome.description: The generation envelope. 'active' is the only status that makes an artifact visible to learners. 'awaiting_approval' is a course run that stopped after storing its outline, waiting for POST /courses/{id}/build.

plan.description: Set for an active course, and for one that stopped at awaiting_approval (the outline being approved). A rejected one returns the chapter report instead of a plan, because nothing that did not verify may be presented as something a learner can start.

chapters.description: What verification measured for a course's exercises, reported for a rejection as well as an activation.

RunEntry.description: One ordered fact from a run. 'kind' names what it is: a provider message the model saw or produced, a function call the model asked for, the tool result the gateway answered it with, or a transport/policy error. 'truncated' and 'redacted' are honest flags: content the entry clipped to fit, or a credential a scrub removed.

seq.description: Position in the run, starting at 0.

ms.description: The provider latency for the turn this entry belongs to.

RunSummary.description: A run without its entries. 'entry_count' is how many entries the run produced; a stored transcript is a prefix when 'truncated' is true.

RunTranscript.description: One generation run's stored conversation, attributed to the run, its kind, its owner, when it ran and how it ended. The owner is the session's own account and does not travel in the body.

AICoursePlan.description: A whole generated course: chapters of markdown teaching, each with verified exercises. Setup belongs to the plan, not to an exercise, because every exercise runs against the same environment.

AICourseSection.description: Authored prose. 'body' is markdown, rendered by the same renderer as the authored courses.

AICourseExercise.description: One exercise of a chapter. It is verified as the challenge artifact the pipeline already understands, so the same rules apply. 'expected' is the engine's own answer, measured during verification and never read from the provider.

AICourseRecord.description: A stored course plus the outcome that admitted it. The owner is the session's account and is not carried in the body.

status.description: The stored record's own state. 'building' is a run writing chapters right now; 'awaiting_approval' is a run paused for the outline (POST /courses/{id}/build continues it); 'interrupted' is a build that stopped without finishing, its verified chapters kept, also continued by the build route; 'active' is a finished course.

base_url.description: Present for openai-compatible. Never present from a boot-configured provider: the config file holds it.

key_set.description: Whether an API key is stored. The key itself never travels back in a body.

preferences.description: The client-owned preference document, or null when the account has none.

PreferencesUpdate.description: The client-owned preference document, stored wholesale under the account's 'ui' key.

provider.description: The provider to run. Accepted aliases normalize on save: an empty string, none and disabled all mean off; deterministic means fake; openai means openai-compatible. The response reports the canonical provider.

key.description: Write-only. Empty keeps the stored key.

timeout_ms.description: Per-call timeout. Zero saves the shipped default (120000).

CourseEditRequest.description: The authored fields a learner may change on a stored course. Every field is optional, at least one must differ from the stored plan, and each chapter entry names a chapter the plan already has.

AIRecordResponse.description: The {ok, challenge} envelope, matching AICourseResponse. One resource-read shape, not two.

AIJobStage.description: One stage of a run as a poller sees it. 'queued' and 'running' exist only in a live view: 'done', 'failed' and 'skipped' are final, and only those three ever appear in an outcome envelope.

AIJob.description: A generation job. While it runs, 'stages' is a live copy of the pipeline's progress; once it finishes, 'stages' is the pipeline's own final report, so a poller and a blocking caller can never be told different things about the same run.

chapters.description: The per-chapter verification report in outline order, one entry per planned chapter, in the same shape the outcome envelope carries it: 'verified', 'dropped', 'refused' or 'skipped', with the exercises the engine ran.

chapters_planned.description: How many chapters the outline planned. A course job only.

chapters_verified.description: How many chapters have passed the engine so far. A course job only.

current_chapter.description: The chapter the gateway has most recently started verifying. It keeps that name until the next chapter is handed in, so it says which chapter the run is on rather than flickering. A course job only.

course_id.description: Present once a course was stored. While the run is still writing chapters it names a 'building' course, which GET /courses/{id} already answers with the chapters that verified; it names the same course once the run activates it. A run that stopped at 'awaiting_approval' names the same building course, which is the index to approve. Absent on a refused run, which stored nothing.

challenge_id.description: Present once an active challenge was stored.

AIJobHandle.description: The job as it is handed back at submission: the id to poll, and what the run is.

AIJobResponse.description: The poll answer. 'job' is null only in the AI-off answer, where there is no job to describe.

AITutorTurn.description: One message in a tutor conversation, oldest first. Role is learner or tutor; text is untrusted and is fenced before the provider sees it.

AITutorContext.description: What the tutor saw, summarised for the drawer. Expected rows appear only after the learner has attempted the exercise; learner_result is ran, error, not_run or unavailable.

AITutorRequest.description: The facts the client sends. The gateway assembles the context and runs the learner's SQL and the reference itself; a client cannot send rows or the assembled context. A conversation must name one exercise source: exercise, or course_id with exercise_id, or challenge_id. A zero-turn hint may omit all three.

exercise.description: The contracts/exercise.schema.json bundle when the exercise is not a stored record.

AIPatchDecision.description: The learner's approval. The patch id comes from the path and the approver from the session, so neither travels in the body.

ProgressSnapshot.description: Any valid JSON value; persisted verbatim.

kind.description: passed, failed, accepted, error, hint or solution.

datasetVersion.description: Content versions this attempt was made against (technical design 7.3).

exerciseVersion.description: Exercise version at the time of the attempt; a later bump marks the attempt as solved on an earlier version.

reason.description: Empty when ready; otherwise why statements cannot run.

version.description: PostgreSQL server version, empty when unavailable.

persistent.description: False when the gateway is on the in-memory store and a restart would lose accounts and progress.

learner.description: Sandbox facts read over the learner connection. Absent when no database is configured.

can_read_app.description: False is correct: learner SQL must not reach gateway metadata. "unknown" means the check could not run.

code.description: Stable gateway error code. The envelope adds non-query codes (NOT_FOUND, the AUTH_* set, ADMIN_REQUIRED and CSRF_REFUSED) to the QueryResult error set.
